mainTopic: Craftsman's hides as מוקצה, the source of the 39 מלאכות, and moving insulating fleece on שבת
overview: The amud opens with a tanner who had his hides brought out on שבת to sit on, which suggests a craftsman's hides are not מוקצה. A ברייתא about a craftsman's boards challenges this. The גמרא answers that boards are different, because a craftsman protects them from damage. A second ברייתא permitting all hides is limited to a homeowner, and the גמרא then shows that the craftsman question is a dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי. Next, the חכמים ask what the 39 אבות מלאכות correspond to. רבי חנינא בר חמא says they match the work of the משכן, and another view says they match the 39 times the word מלאכה appears in the תורה. רב יוסף asks whether the יוסף verse is part of that count, and the question ends in תיקו. A ברייתא then supports the משכן view, including how carrying is learned from moving the משכן's boards. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה about wool fleece. רבא says fleece used for insulating may be moved, and a new student challenges him from the משנה; the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The tanner who had hides brought to sit on
steps.stepSummary: The speaker says his father was a tanner and had hides brought on שבת so people could sit on them. This shows a craftsman's hides may be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: My father was a tanner, and he said: Bring hides and we will sit on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The speaker uses his father's practice as evidence. Even a professional tanner's hides, which are his work materials, may be moved on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we might think a craftsman's work materials are מוקצה, because he keeps them for his trade and does not use them for anything else. Yet this tanner told people to sit on his hides. That suggests hides are not set aside the way other materials are, so moving them is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A tanner, someone who processes animal hides
Hides, animal skins
A craftsman or professional

phrases.english: My father was a tanner,
and he said: Bring hides
and we will sit on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion on the previous amud about whether hides may be moved on שבת.
steps.raayaObject: A craftsman's hides may be moved on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A practice: the speaker's father, a tanner, had hides brought to sit on during שבת.

steps.title: Challenge from a craftsman's boards
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a craftsman's boards may not be moved on שבת unless he intended them for a use like serving guests. This seems to contradict moving a tanner's hides.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: A homeowner's boards may be moved, but a craftsman's boards may not be moved. If he planned to put bread on them for guests, either kind may be moved!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks Step 1 with a ברייתא. A craftsman's work materials, like boards, may not be moved on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא draws a clear line. A homeowner's boards are fine to move, but a craftsman's boards are מוקצה because they are kept for his trade. If the same rule applies to hides, the tanner's hides should also be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Wooden boards or planks
A homeowner, an ordinary person who is not a craftsman
One may move them
He intended or designated

phrases.english: They challenged:
Boards belonging to a homeowner,
one may move them,
but those of a craftsman, one may not move them.
And if he intended to place on them
bread for guests,
in either case one may move them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from the tanner's practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a craftsman's hides may be moved.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A craftsman's boards are forbidden to move, so a craftsman's hides should be forbidden too.

steps.title: Boards are different because the craftsman cares about them
steps.stepSummary: Boards are different. A craftsman is careful with them so they will not get damaged, so he sets them aside completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Boards are different, because one is particular about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by separating boards from hides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A craftsman worries that his boards will be scratched or ruined, so he keeps them away from any other use. That makes them מוקצה. Sitting on hides does not damage them, so the tanner does not mind other uses, and they may be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
He is particular or careful about it

phrases.english: Boards are different,
because one is particular about them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from boards.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All of a craftsman's materials are מוקצה in the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only materials the craftsman protects from damage are set aside. Hides are not, so they may be moved.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the key reason for this kind of מוקצה: whether the owner is careful to keep the item away from other uses.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא permitting all hides
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says all hides, tanned or untanned, may be moved on שבת. Tanning matters only for טומאה. The גמרא suggests this includes a craftsman's hides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Hides, whether tanned or untanned, may be moved on שבת. They mentioned tanned hides only for טומאה. Doesn't this mean there is no difference between a homeowner's and a craftsman's hides?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to support moving a craftsman's hides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא permits moving all hides and makes only one distinction, tanned versus untanned, and only for טומאה. Since it does not separate a homeowner from a craftsman, the גמרא suggests it permits a craftsman's hides too.

keyTerms.meaning: Tanned or processed (hides)
Ritual impurity
Is it not so that...? (suggests a reading)
There is no difference

steps.confusionAlert: Tanned versus untanned matters for טומאה, because only a finished hide counts as a usable item that can become טמא. It does not matter for moving on שבת.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹרוֹת, בֵּין עֲבוּדִין וּבֵין שֶׁאֵין עֲבוּדִין,
phrases.english: Hides, whether tanned or not tanned,
it is permitted to move them on Shabbat.
They mentioned tanned hides
only with regard to ritual impurity.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לַָאו לָא שְׁנָא שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: What, is it not that there is no difference whether a homeowner's,
and no difference whether a craftsman's?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second source on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: A craftsman's hides may be moved on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that permits moving all hides without separating owners.

steps.title: The ברייתא speaks only of a homeowner
steps.stepSummary: No, the ברייתא is talking only about a homeowner's hides.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it refers to a homeowner's hides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by limiting the ברייתא to a homeowner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is only about a homeowner, it says nothing about a craftsman. A craftsman's hides could still be forbidden.

phrases.english: No, it refers to those of a homeowner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide the law for a craftsman.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be speaking only about a homeowner.

steps.title: Why didn't the ברייתא state the craftsman exception?
steps.stepSummary: If a craftsman's hides are forbidden, the ברייתא should have said so, just as it spelled out the טומאה distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for a craftsman's hides, what is the law? They may not be moved? If so, the ברייתא taught that tanned hides differ only for טומאה. It should have made a distinction within its own case: When does this apply? To a homeowner's hides, but not to a craftsman's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the limit made in Step 5. If a craftsman's hides really were forbidden, the ברייתא would have said so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא bothered to spell out one distinction, the one about טומאה. So if a craftsman's hides were forbidden on שבת, it should also have said 'this applies only to a homeowner.' Its silence suggests no such exception exists.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let it distinguish and teach
Within its own topic
In what case is this said?

phrases.english: But a craftsman's hides, what is the law?
They may not be moved?
If so, that which was taught:
They mentioned tanned hides
only with regard to ritual impurity,
let it distinguish and teach within its own case:
In what case is this said?
For those of a homeowner,
but for those of a craftsman, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אבל של אומן מאי אין מטלטלין אי הכי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit made in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא refers only to a homeowner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא spelled out the טומאה distinction, so it should also have spelled out a homeowner/craftsman distinction if one existed.

steps.title: The whole ברייתא is about a homeowner
steps.stepSummary: The entire ברייתא deals only with a homeowner, so a craftsman never came up.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole ברייתא is speaking about a homeowner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends Step 5. The ברייתא's whole topic is a homeowner, so it had no reason to mention a craftsman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding the טומאה note was a small side comment about hides in general. Bringing in a craftsman would mean introducing a whole new kind of owner that the ברייתא was not discussing. So its silence proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, the entire teaching
It is speaking about

steps.whatToRemember: The tanner's practice shows a craftsman's hides are not מוקצה, since he does not mind people using them, unlike boards. The ברייתא permitting all hides is limited to a homeowner, so it neither proves nor disproves the craftsman's case.

phrases.english: The whole of it is speaking about a homeowner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the scope of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's silence about a craftsman means there is no exception for a craftsman.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא never addressed a craftsman, so its silence teaches nothing about him.

steps.title: The hides question is an old dispute among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that whether a craftsman's hides may be moved on שבת is a dispute between תנאים. The first opinion forbids it, and רבי יוסי permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of תנאים: A homeowner's hides may be moved on שבת, but a craftsman's hides may not be moved. רבי יוסי says: both kinds may be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the hides discussion. It shows that the question is already argued about in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 4-7 went back and forth over whether a craftsman's hides are מוקצה. Here the גמרא brings a ברייתא where the first opinion (the תנא קמא) forbids moving a craftsman's hides, but רבי יוסי allows it. So both sides of our discussion have support from תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute between תנאים, meaning this question was already argued about in the time of the משנה
A homeowner, a regular person who is not a professional
A craftsman, a professional who works with the material
May be moved or carried around (within a permitted area) on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: The question of a craftsman's hides is a dispute. The תנא קמא forbids moving them, since the craftsman sets them aside for his work. רבי יוסי permits moving them.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute of Tannaim:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹרוֹת שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת מְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתָן,
phrases.english: Hides of a homeowner, one may move them,
but those of a craftsman, one may not move them.
Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה מְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתָן.
phrases.english: Both this and that, one may move them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the hides discussion by showing that the question is a dispute between תנאים
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A craftsman's hides: the תנא קמא forbids moving them on שבת, and רבי יוסי permits it.

steps.title: Where does the number 39 come from?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים sit again and ask: the משנה says there are 39 main categories of labor. What does that number correspond to?
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat again and asked: What we learned in the משנה, 'The main categories of labor are forty minus one,' what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. The חכמים ask what the 39 main forbidden labors of שבת are based on. This line sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in the seventh פרק of שבת counts exactly 39 אבות מלאכות. The question is not what the labors are. It is why the list has exactly 39 and what source it matches.

keyTerms.meaning: They sat again, meaning the same group returned to discuss something
They had a question or were unsure about something
The main categories of labor forbidden on שבת
What does it correspond to? What is the number based on?

phrases.english: They sat again and raised a question:
That which we learned in the Mishnah:
The main categories of labor are forty minus one,
what do they correspond to?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same group of חכמים moves on to a new question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the number 39 for the אבות מלאכות is based on

steps.title: The 39 labors match the work of the משכן
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר חמא answers that the 39 labors correspond to the kinds of work done in building the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר חמא said to them: They correspond to the labors of the משכן.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer is given. The forbidden labors of שבת are the same kinds of work that were done for the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each kind of work used to build the משכן counts as a main labor for שבת. A kind of work that was not done in the משכן is not on the list, even if it is hard or important.

keyTerms.meaning: The kinds of work done to build and prepare the משכן

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the well-known rule that the מלאכות of שבת are learned from the משכן.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר חָמָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Chama said to them:
They correspond to the labors of the Mishkan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 39 labors match the kinds of work done in the משכן

steps.title: The 39 labors match the times 'labor' is written in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן ברבי אלעזר quotes רבי שמעון ברבי יוסי בן לקוניא. He says the number 39 matches how many times the words 'labor,' 'his labor,' and 'the labor of' appear in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן ברבי אלעזר said to them: This is what רבי שמעון ברבי יוסי בן לקוניא said: They correspond to the words 'labor,' 'his labor,' and 'the labor of' in the תורה, which appear forty minus one times.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer is given. The number 39 comes from counting how many times the word for labor appears in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer explains the number 39 by counting words in the text. The first answer explained it by looking at the work done in the משכן.

keyTerms.meaning: Labor or work
His labor or his work
The labor of (the joined form, used before another noun)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan son of Rabbi Elazar said to them,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן לָקוֹנְיָא:
phrases.english: thus said Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Yosei ben Lakonya:
They correspond to 'labor,' 'his labor,' and 'the labor of'
that appear in the Torah forty minus one times.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The number 39 matches how many times the forms of the word מלאכה appear in the תורה

steps.title: Does the verse about יוסף count?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks whether the word 'his labor' in the story of יוסף ('he came into the house to do his labor') is part of the count of 39.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked: 'And he came into the house to do his labor.' Is that included in the count or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks a follow-up question about the second answer. Should one specific verse be counted in the 39?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the number 39 comes from counting words, every case of the word matters. The verse about יוסף and the wife of פוטיפר is unclear, because 'his labor' there might not mean real work. So we do not know whether it belongs in the count.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked, raised a question he could not answer
Part of the count

phrases.english: Rav Yosef asked:
'And he came into the house to do his labor,'
is it part of the count, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question about the word-count answer in step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether מלאכתו in the יוסף story counts toward the 39

steps.title: אביי: just bring a ספר תורה and count
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that they can bring a ספר תורה and count. If there are 39 without this verse, it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Let us bring a ספר תורה and count.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's question. Why be unsure? Just count the words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the total without this verse is 39, it is not part of the count. If the total is only 39 when this verse is included, it is part of the count. A simple count settles the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us bring
And let us count

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Let us bring a Torah scroll and count!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב יוסף's question by pointing out that a simple count would settle it
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Count the words in a ספר תורה to settle it
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's question of whether the יוסף verse is part of the count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A count of the words in a ספר תורה would show whether the verse is needed to reach 39, so there is no reason to be unsure.

steps.title: A precedent: they once counted from a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: אביי supports his idea. רבה בר בר חנה quoted רבי יוחנן that in a similar case, they did not leave until they brought a ספר תורה and counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבה בר בר חנה say in the name of רבי יוחנן: They did not move from there until they brought a ספר תורה and counted them!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי backs up his suggestion. He shows that the חכמים once settled a counting question exactly this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting words in a ספר תורה to settle a question is not a new idea. There is a precedent from the time of רבי יוחנן, so אביי asks why we would not do the same here.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't (someone) say? Used to bring a supporting statement
They did not move from there
And they counted them

steps.confusionAlert: אביי's idea sounds like it closes the question. But the next passage will explain why simply counting may not work for רב יוסף. Wait for that before thinking the matter is settled.

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: Didn't Rabba bar bar Chana say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
They did not move from there
until they brought a Torah scroll and counted them!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's suggestion with a precedent
steps.raayaObject: That a counting question can be settled by counting in a ספר תורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן: they brought a ספר תורה and counted

steps.title: רב יוסף explains why counting won't settle it: the first possibility
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains why counting alone does not help. Another verse, 'וְהַמְּלָאכָה הָיְתָה דַיָּם', is also unclear. If that verse is in the count, then the יוסף verse is not about real work.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The reason I am unsure is that it is written, 'And the labor was enough for them.' Maybe that verse is part of the count. Then the verse about יוסף follows the one who said he went into the house to take care of his own needs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי's idea of counting. He shows that his doubt is really about two verses, and this step gives the first side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting gives the number 39 only if we already know which verses to include. רב יוסף has two unclear verses, and only one of them can be part of the 39. The first side says the משכן verse counts, so the word 'his labor' in the יוסף verse is not about real work. It is a polite way of describing something else.

keyTerms.meaning: I am unsure / it is a doubt for me
'And the labor was enough for them' (a verse about the משכן)
from the count, meaning part of the 39
his personal needs (a gentle way of describing something private)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי's 'go count' sounds like it should end the question. It does not. Counting tells you the total, but it cannot tell you which of two doubtful verses is the one that belongs in the 39.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי קָא מְסַפְּקָא לִי
phrases.english: He said to him: The reason I am unsure
is because it is written: 'And the labor was enough for them'
phrases.notes: שמות לו:ז, about the materials for the משכן

phrases.english: Is this verse part of the count?
And then that verse (about יוסף) follows the one who said
that he went in to take care of his own needs.
phrases.notes: So the יוסף verse is not about real work

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי קָא מְסַפְּקָא לִי מִשּׁוּם דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אביי's suggestion of counting by showing why counting cannot settle the doubt
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the two unclear verses belongs in the count of 39: the משכן verse or the יוסף verse?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing why the proposed method cannot resolve the doubt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Counting the words in a ספר תורה would settle whether the יוסף verse belongs in the 39.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two doubtful verses, the משכן verse and the יוסף verse, and only one of them fits into the 39. Counting cannot tell which one.

steps.title: The second possibility: the יוסף verse counts instead
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the יוסף verse is in the count. In that case, the משכן verse means only that the gathering of materials was finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe 'He came into the house to do his labor' is part of the count. Then the verse 'And the labor was enough for them' means that the job was complete.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the other side of his doubt. This time the יוסף verse is about real work, and the משכן verse is read differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this side, יוסף really went in to do his work, so his verse is part of the count. The משכן verse is then not about doing מלאכה at all. It only says the bringing of materials was finished. Each reading leaves exactly one of the two verses inside the count.

keyTerms.meaning: or perhaps (introduces the other side of a doubt)
this is what it means
that the work was finished

phrases.english: Or perhaps, 'He came into the house
to do his labor' is part of the count,
and this verse, 'And the labor was enough for them',
means this: that the work was completed for them.
phrases.notes: Only the gathering of materials was done, not actual מלאכה

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא ״וַיָּבֹא הַבַּיְתָה לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתּוֹ״ מִמִּנְיָנָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the same doubt
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the יוסף verse, rather than the משכן verse, belongs in the count

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot decide, so it ends with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it cannot decide between the two sides. The question is left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no answer was found. We still know the total is 39. We just do not know which of the two verses fills that spot.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand (the question is left unresolved)

steps.whatToRemember: Counting the word מלאכה gives 39. It cannot tell us whether the יוסף verse or the משכן verse is the one included, so the question ends with תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב יוסף's question without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The doubt about which verse is included in the count stays unresolved.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the view that the labors come from the משכן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבי חנינא בר חמא's view. You are liable only for a מלאכה that had a matching kind of work in the משכן, such as sowing and reaping.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that follows the one who said the 39 match the work of the משכן. The ברייתא says: A person is liable only for a kind of work that had a match in the משכן. They sowed, so you may not sow. They reaped, so you may not reap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the two answers from steps 10–11. It brings a ברייתא that backs the first answer: the 39 מלאכות come from the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets a clear rule: liability on שבת depends on whether that kind of work was done in the משכן. 'They' are the people who built the משכן, and 'you' are every Jew on שבת. For example, they grew plants to make dyes for the משכן, so sowing is a מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא was taught in line with the one who said
the kinds of work done in building the משכן
something like it, a matching kind
one is liable only for

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule behind all of הלכות שבת: the משכן is the model that defines what counts as a מלאכה.

phrases.english: It was taught in line with the one who said
that they correspond to the work of the Mishkan.
As it was taught: One is liable only

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְלָאכָה שֶׁכַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהּ הָיְתָה בַּמִּשְׁכָּן.
phrases.english: for a labor whose match existed in the Mishkan.
They sowed, so you may not sow.
They reaped, so you may not reap.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר כְּנֶגֶד עֲבוֹדוֹת הַמִּשְׁכָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the counting question and returns to the two opinions about where the number 39 comes from
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא בר חמא's view that the 39 מלאכות correspond to the work of the משכן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that ties liability to work that had a match in the משכן

steps.title: Carrying is learned from moving the משכן's boards
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Lifting the boards from the ground onto the wagon, lowering them back down, and passing them from wagon to wagon are the sources for different kinds of carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: They lifted the boards from the ground onto the wagon, so you may not bring things in from the public area to a private area. They lowered the boards from the wagon to the ground, so you may not take things out from a private area to the public area. They passed things from wagon to wagon, so you may not take things from one private area to another private area.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps listing examples. Now it shows how the different kinds of carrying come from the way the boards of the משכן were moved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The desert floor is treated like רשות הרבים, and each wagon is like a רשות היחיד. Lifting a board onto a wagon is bringing something in. Lowering it to the ground is taking something out. The last example, private area to private area, sounds strange because that is not usually forbidden, and the גמרא will deal with it next.

keyTerms.meaning: the wooden boards of the משכן
wagon (treated as a private area)
public area
private area
take out / bring in

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think carrying from one private area to another is a simple, clear איסור. The ברייתא says it here, but the גמרא is about to ask what that line really means.

phrases.aramaic: הֵם הֶעֱלוּ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁים מִקַּרְקַע לַעֲגָלָה,
phrases.english: They lifted the boards from the ground onto the wagon,
phrases.notes: Ground = public area; wagon = private area

phrases.english: so you may not bring in
from the public area to a private area.

phrases.aramaic: הֵם הוֹרִידוּ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁים מֵעֲגָלָה לְקַרְקַע,
phrases.english: They lowered the boards from the wagon to the ground,
so you may not take out
from a private area to the public area.
They passed things out from wagon to wagon,
so you may not take out
from one private area to another private area.
phrases.notes: The גמרא will question this next

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵם הֶעֱלוּ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁים מִקַּרְקַע לַעֲגָלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with examples about carrying
steps.raayaObject: That the מלאכה of carrying also comes from the משכן
steps.raayaSupportSource: How the boards of the משכן were moved between the ground and the wagons

steps.title: What work is done between two private domains?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is puzzled by the last part of the ברייתא. What forbidden work is done by moving something from one רשות היחיד to another?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you move something from one private domain to another private domain, what forbidden work are you doing?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא said that passing boards from one wagon to another was the source for a kind of carrying. The גמרא asks how that can be, since each wagon is a private domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden work of carrying is moving an object between a private domain and a public domain. Moving something from one private domain to another private domain does not seem to cross into public space at all. So the גמרא wants to know what forbidden work this case could possibly teach.

keyTerms.meaning: A private domain (here, each wagon)
What is he doing? (what forbidden work is this?)

phrases.english: From a private domain to a private domain
phrases.notes: Quoting the end of the ברייתא about passing boards from wagon to wagon

phrases.english: what [forbidden work] is he doing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the last case in the ברייתא from Step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What forbidden work is involved in moving an object between two private domains?

steps.title: The object passes over a public domain
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא, or some say רב אדא בר אהבה, explain the case. The object goes from one private domain to another by passing through a public domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both said, and some say it was רב אדא בר אהבה: it means moving from one private domain to another private domain by way of the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 20. The space between the two wagons was public space, and the boards were handed across it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two wagons were private domains, but the ground between them was a public domain. So passing a board from one wagon to the other carried it through public space. That gives a source for liability when an object passes over a public domain on its way between two private domains.

keyTerms.meaning: A public domain (here, the space between the wagons)
By way of, passing through
Both of them

steps.whatToRemember: Passing boards from wagon to wagon in the משכן teaches carrying from one private domain to another through a public domain.

phrases.english: It was Abaye and Rava, who both said,
and some say it was Rav Adda bar Ahava:
from a private domain to a private domain
by way of the public domain.
phrases.notes: The space between the wagons was a public domain

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is passing an object between two private domains through a public domain, like the space between the wagons.

steps.title: רבא limits the ban on moving fleece
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which says one may insulate food in wool fleece but may not move the fleece. רבא says this applies only to fleece that was not used for insulating. Fleece that was used for insulating may be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: food may be insulated in wool fleece, and one may not move it. רבא said: this was taught only where he did not insulate food in the fleece. But if he did insulate food in it, he may move it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line of the משנה about wool fleece. רבא explains when the ban on moving the fleece applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw wool fleece is usually kept for sale or for making cloth, so on שבת it counts as מוקצה, something not meant for use. רבא holds that if a person used the fleece to insulate food, he showed that he plans to use it. Then it is no longer מוקצה and may be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: Wool fleece (raw shorn wool)
One may move (an object on שבת)
He insulated (wrapped food to keep it warm)
They only taught this in the case of (a limiting formula)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רבא's rule that using an object for a שבת purpose can take it out of the category of מוקצה.

phrases.english: [The משנה said: one may insulate] in wool fleece, and one may not move [it].
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, which the גמרא is now explaining

phrases.english: Rava said: they taught this only
where he did not insulate [food] in them,
but if he insulated [food] in them,
one may move them.
phrases.notes: Using the fleece for insulating shows he intends to use it on שבת

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the 39 kinds of work and returns to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on moving wool fleece applies only if it was not used for insulating; fleece used for insulating may be moved.

steps.title: A new student challenges רבא from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: A scholar on his first day in the study hall challenges רבא. The משנה itself speaks of fleece used for insulating and still says it may not be moved. So how does the person get the food out?
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain scholar, on his first day, raised an objection to רבא: 'One may insulate in wool fleece, and one may not move it.' So how does he act?
steps.whatsHappening: A new student attacks רבא's rule using the words of the משנה. The question at the end sets up the next move, which will explain how the pot is taken out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'one may insulate in fleece' and right after says 'one may not move it.' That reads like it is talking about fleece that was already used for insulating, which goes against רבא. The משנה then asks how he gets the pot out, and its answer on the next amud, a workaround that avoids moving the fleece directly, shows the fleece is still forbidden to move.

keyTerms.meaning: On his first day (a newcomer to the study hall)
One may insulate (food)
How does he act?

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'כיצד הוא עושה' are not the student's own rhetorical question. They are part of the source he quotes, which asks how one removes the pot and then answers it (on the next amud: he lifts off the cover and the fleece falls away). The attack is that the source needs this workaround at all. That shows fleece already used for insulating still may not be moved directly.

phrases.english: A certain one of the Sages raised an objection
on his first day, to Rava:
One may insulate in wool fleece
and one may not move them.
phrases.notes: The same משנה seems to forbid moving fleece that was used for insulating

phrases.english: How, then, does he act?
phrases.notes: Still part of the quote. The answer comes on the next amud: how he takes out the pot without moving the fleece directly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ הַהוּא מֵרַבָּנָן בַּר יוֹמֵיהּ לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's rule from Step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that fleece used for insulating may be moved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה speaks of fleece that was used for insulating, yet it says the fleece may not be moved and describes how to remove the pot without moving it. That contradicts רבא's claim that insulated fleece may be moved.
